guard_streams.source: Ofcom residential and small-business contract rules

facts.detail: Residential and small-business customers with ten employees or fewer should receive a one-page contract summary, or three pages for bundled services, before consent.
The summary includes key information such as charges, contract length and cancellation process.
The provider must also supply more detailed contract information in writing before the customer is bound.
The required written information precedes valid consent to enter the contract.

guard_streams.write_limit: Pre-contract documents are commercial evidence and cannot prove physical availability at a postcode or parcel.

facts.detail: Providers may change contract terms but must generally give at least one month's notice.
A customer should have a penalty-free exit right where a notified change does not benefit them.
Contract terms, including price arrangements, must be fair and transparent.
The protection concerns contract changes rather than network-build or serviceability evidence.

guard_streams.write_limit: Contract-change rights must remain separate from parcel coverage and speed fields.

guard_streams.source: Ofcom business contract guidance updated 26 June 2026

facts.detail: Businesses can request clear information on service limits or restrictions.
Contract information can include minimum service-quality levels and initial connection time.
Customer-service and maintenance arrangements can be specified in the contract.
Contract length, renewal conditions and termination charges can be required in clear form.

guard_streams.write_limit: Contractual service-quality commitments are not observed parcel performance.

guard_streams.source: Ofcom Q4 2025 complaints publication dated 11 May 2026

facts.detail: The publication covers complaints received from October to December 2025.
Overall complaints increased on the previous quarter for the first time since 2023.
Broadband and landline complaint rates decreased while mobile complaints increased.
The comparison covers major providers and is not a complete premises-level service inventory.

guard_streams.write_limit: Provider complaint rates must not be applied to individual postcode or parcel confidence.

facts.detail: The Spring 2026 update was published on 13 May 2026.
Fixed broadband availability is a January 2026 snapshot.
The fixed reporting scope includes fixed-line and fixed wireless access networks.
Data collected for the report was also used to update Ofcom's coverage checkers.

guard_streams.write_limit: A dated national snapshot is not continuous live parcel telemetry.

facts.detail: Full fibre was reported available to 24.9 million residential premises, representing 82% of UK homes.
Gigabit-capable availability was reported at 27.1 million homes, or 89%.
Ofcom reported 39,000 premises unable to access decent broadband through fixed line or FWA.
The number without affordable decent broadband was reported at 4,000 after accounting for selected lower-priced satellite services.

guard_streams.write_limit: National headline counts and percentages cannot populate exact parcel availability.

facts.detail: Full-fibre and gigabit coverage headlines focus on residential properties.
Full-fibre take-up is reported across residential and commercial premises.
Some commercial premises potentially meeting USO criteria may already use leased lines and were not counted as eligible.
Lower-priced satellite packages were available only in selected areas and marketed as residential products.

guard_streams.write_limit: Residential products and aggregate eligibility cannot prove exact commercial-parcel service.

facts.detail: Fixed broadband coverage downloads describe maximum available speeds.
Performance reporting concerns active-connection speeds and is considered robust to local-authority level.
Ofcom has not published a fixed-performance postcode file since the July 2024 methodology revision.
Ofcom does not consider the revised performance analysis sufficiently robust for postcode publication.

guard_streams.write_limit: Coverage availability must not be relabelled as measured performance.

facts.detail: The planned-deployment report examines anticipated very-high-capacity coverage through the end of 2028.
It is based on operator deployment plans as of January 2026.
The report includes privately funded and publicly supported operator plans.
The forward-looking report supplements, rather than replaces, the January 2026 current-coverage snapshot.

guard_streams.write_limit: Planned deployment cannot promote a current parcel candidate.

facts.detail: Ofcom material may generally be reproduced free of charge when accurate, acknowledged and not used misleadingly, subject to stated ownership conditions.
Ofcom provides website material as-is without guarantees of currency or accuracy.
Ofcom does not guarantee uninterrupted functions, error-free operation or permanent link availability.
Reused material should acknowledge Ofcom copyright and identify the publication.

guard_streams.write_limit: Licence permission does not relax source-date, acceptance or provenance controls.

facts.detail: The July 2026 contract-progress page was updated on 20 July 2026.
The table is a snapshot of BDUK data held on 16 July 2026.
Figures are rounded to the nearest ten and may not sum due to rounding.
Variable delay between delivery and BDUK ingestion means the table should not assess contractual milestones.

guard_streams.write_limit: Rounded management information is not exact parcel-ready evidence.

facts.detail: Contracted-premises figures include only the initial contract scope.
Deferred-scope premises may not be represented.
Contract-management figures are not directly comparable with BDUK official statistics.
The management table tracks supplier delivery to contracted premises, while official statistics measure connections resulting from subsidy.

guard_streams.write_limit: Contract scope and built counts cannot substitute for exact current address serviceability.

facts.detail: The July table reports a rounded total of 838,490 contracted premises.
It reports a rounded total of 287,510 built contracted premises.
The Cheshire call-off row showed 18,460 contracted and zero built premises in this snapshot.
Central Cornwall showed 6,940 contracted and 6,940 built contracted premises in the snapshot.

guard_streams.write_limit: Contract-level examples are programme snapshots and cannot identify individual covered parcels.

guard_streams.source: Official Ofcom Spring 2026 ZIP endpoint and current environment

facts.detail: The official outer archive path is 202601_fixed_broadband_coverage_and_full_fibre_take-up-r1.zip with version query 422620.
The endpoint responds as application/x-zip-compressed.
The web fetch layer rejects the binary content type and returns no persisted archive bytes.
A fresh controlled container download attempt also failed, so no archive signature, hash or member inventory was claimed.

guard_streams.write_limit: A confirmed URL is not an accepted archive; exact bytes, hashes, CRCs, schema and row counts remain mandatory.

facts.detail: No live owner lease was found before publication.
No active or over-15-minute PENDING execution was found.
The existing task ID and continuation key were retained without starting a second runner.
No candidate, measured-speed row or 3-of-4 accuracy record was promoted without the accepted r2 join.

guard_streams.write_limit: The final operation remains blocked until canonical Windows host script 024 produces validated archive and postjoin evidence.
